storage.subject: storage.application_pvc
storage.kubernetes_effect: the application is stateless: it writes no local persistent files and keeps all state in the database. The Deployment needs no PVC/volumeMount. Database persistence is a SEPARATE concern handled by the (external/managed) DB, not the app.

runtime_dependencies.subject: database.default
runtime_dependencies.kubernetes_effect: default profile uses an in-process, in-memory database. Data is ephemeral and per-replica; suitable for dev/demo only. Do NOT run this in production — choose an external database (postgres/mysql profile).

runtime_dependencies.subject: database.profile.mysql
runtime_dependencies.kubernetes_effect: 'mysql' profile connects to an external MySQL. Provide the JDBC URL via ConfigMap and credentials via Secret; ensure network reachability from the cluster.

runtime_dependencies.subject: database.profile.postgres
runtime_dependencies.kubernetes_effect: 'postgres' profile connects to an external PostgreSQL. Provide the JDBC URL via ConfigMap and credentials via Secret; ensure network reachability from the cluster.

startup_order.subject: startup.order
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: overall ordering: DB -> migration Job -> seed -> application Deployments

startup_order.subject: startup.sql_init
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: Spring SQL init runs schema/data scripts in-process at application startup (basic script init), NOT a separate migration Job.

startup_order.subject: startup.migration_tool
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: no versioned migration tool (Flyway/Liquibase) is on the classpath, so there is no dedicated migration Job/initContainer; schema/data are applied in-process at startup.

startup_order.subject: startup.sql_init.mode.mysql
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: 'mysql' profile forces SQL init to run even against the external DB (mode=always); it re-runs on every pod start.

startup_order.subject: startup.sql_init.mode.postgres
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: 'postgres' profile forces SQL init to run even against the external DB (mode=always); it re-runs on every pod start.

startup_order.subject: startup.sql_init.idempotent
startup_order.value: 3 schema script(s) use IF (NOT) EXISTS guards
startup_order.kubernetes_effect: schema DDL is guarded (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / DROP TABLE IF EXISTS), so startup SQL init re-runs safely on each pod start; no one-shot migration Job is required.

health_checks.subject: health.actuator
health_checks.kubernetes_effect: exposes /actuator/health and the Kubernetes liveness/readiness health groups

health_checks.subject: health.exposure
health_checks.kubernetes_effect: controls which /actuator/* endpoints are reachable over HTTP

health_checks.subject: health.liveness_probe
health_checks.kubernetes_effect: livenessProbe httpGet path candidate on port 8080. Spring Boot auto-enables the liveness health group when running under Kubernetes.

health_checks.subject: health.readiness_probe
health_checks.kubernetes_effect: readinessProbe httpGet path candidate on port 8080. Spring Boot auto-enables the readiness health group when running under Kubernetes.

health_checks.subject: health.additional_paths
health_checks.kubernetes_effect: use /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness by default. Only probe /livez and /readyz if you enable add-additional-paths=true (e.g. via env/ConfigMap).

container_image.subject: image.dockerfile
container_image.kubernetes_effect: no Dockerfile — but this does NOT mean the app cannot be containerised (see bootBuildImage)

container_image.subject: image.buildpack_support
container_image.kubernetes_effect: the Spring Boot Gradle plugin provides `bootBuildImage`, which builds an OCI image with Cloud Native Buildpacks — no Dockerfile needed.

container_image.subject: image.build_command
container_image.kubernetes_effect: builds the container image via buildpacks (requires a Docker daemon or rootless builder)

container_image.subject: image.build_strategy
container_image.kubernetes_effect: buildpacks auto-detect the JDK/JRE and layer the app for you (reproducible, maintained base images); a Dockerfile gives full control but you own the base image and CVE patching.

container_image.subject: image.runs_as_nonroot
container_image.value: buildpack image runs as non-root by default
container_image.kubernetes_effect: Paketo/Spring buildpack images run as the non-root `cnb` user, so securityContext.runAsNonRoot is satisfied when built via bootBuildImage (still set it explicitly).
